_about: The pipeline of every Lemo-Opuscar style (the 6 stages of every style), with prompts for a film drawn in code as a render(t) page inside HyperFrames. Read by packages/style-catalog for the styles under pins.lemo. Derived from General Style's pipeline in config/styles.json; the sound comes from the app (no Lemo-Opuscar audio).

pipeline.title: Prepare
pipeline.what: Brief, files read and what the style needs; Claude asks only what is missing

action.label: Prepare
action.prompt: Read the brief, the answers from the New project dialog and what the app found in my files (its scan). Write BRIEF.md in a few short lines: who the film speaks to, the one thing it says ("This film tells [audience] that [promise]."), what must be in it (the names, facts and lines the brief gives) and the length and format New project set. Do not ask what the dialog already answered. Write ASSETS.md: each file I gave, what it is, where the film can use it, what is missing. The look, motion, camera and sound come from the style's STYLE.md: keep all of it; the story is this brief's own. When the style cuts from real material (your rules say so), gather it now, before the treatment, as your rules say (§3a: my files first, then the sources the style names, with the demo's material tools; say what you will fetch, from where and under which licence; every item in CREDITS, every fact in FACTS.md) and list it in ASSETS.md. When I gave no files at all and the style draws everything in code, go on without asking. Every conflict (the brief against this style's own design or what it can draw, against the New project fields) and every missing thing the brief needs (a file, a link, a logo it names) goes in one message as moworks-studio §2b says (what each side says, two or three choices, your suggestion first), and then stop without writing BRIEF.md: the owner answers in the chat. Write BRIEF.md last. Change nothing in the film yet; then stop.

pipeline.title: Storyboard
pipeline.what: One treatment of the brief in the style, drawn with real code as an image board; you approve it or ask for another

action.label: Write
action.prompt: Make one storyboard option as your rules say (the Lemo-Opuscar treatment: one subject, one goal, one turn; a hook in the first 3 seconds; one native move of the style at the peak): one structure for this brief, boards/A, with its STORYBOARD.md (every frame one shot with its own seconds) and a posed index.html whose frames are drawn with the style's real drawing code (a render(t) page, as your rules say), timed to the voice-over when there is one. Do not open the style's demo film or its DEMO.md yet. After writing or changing the boards, call the app's board_stills tool once: it checks the boards and returns the option's sheets (3 × 3 frames). Read the sheets once; fix only a real problem, then call it again with only the frames you changed (at most once more). Then stop: I approve it in the Storyboard dialog or ask there for another option; when I choose one, write it to STORYBOARD.md and stop for my approval.

pipeline.title: Motion Plan
pipeline.what: How every shot moves: the style's camera grammar and native moves, with numbers; you approve

action.label: Write
action.prompt: Write the Motion Plan for every shot of the approved plan into MOTION-PLAN.json (the motion plan format in your instructions): concrete numbers, not adjectives. The film's motion is drawn in code as the style's STYLE.md says (motion quality, camera grammar, native moves): cite those rows as source {"kind": "style", "id": "STYLE.md §<n> <move>"}; a Motion Library item only for an HTML layer on top of the canvas (a title, an end card), or new. Give every held element, the background, the camera and every character its always-on row with numbers (moworks-alive §2), each shot its "says" line in my language (what moves and how strongly, words I can judge) and the plan its "approving" line. Write only MOTION-PLAN.json: no composition and no index.html (the Build writes the film once). Then stop for my approval in the Motion Plan dialog.

pipeline.title: Build
pipeline.what: The film built as one render(t) page in the style, inside HyperFrames

action.label: Build
action.prompt: Build the film of the approved storyboard to the approved Motion Plan as your rules say (a Lemo-Opuscar page inside HyperFrames: window.render(t), window.READY, the app's bridge; the style's demo source is in .moworks/library/lemo/ to learn its techniques, never its story, shots or timeline), timed to the voice-over when there is one. Write no sound effects or music: the app adds them after your Review. Keep every element on screen, the background, the camera and every character moving between the moves, as the studio's moworks-alive rule says (nothing still for more than 2 s except the final logo hold; the brief's motion words become that motion).

pipeline.title: Review
pipeline.what: Claude looks at stills of the film like a strict director: seven scores, fixes, until every score is 8 or more

action.label: Review
action.prompt: Run the Review as the Moworks QC rules say (the Moworks QC file named in your rules): call the app's qc_sheets tool for each round, read the sheets, score the seven criteria (Motion against the moworks-alive rule: its numbers, MOTION-PLAN.json's always-on rows and the app's still-stretch check when there is one), fix the 3 worst problems (open only the code of the shots the sheets flag, once each; Grep, then Edit) and every layout or contrast error of HyperFrames' check; 1 to 3 rounds, stop as soon as every score is 8 or more; after 3 rounds say why. Score only what you saw after your last change: a round that ends with a fix takes the sheets once more before the final score. Write every round to QC-REVIEW.md and end the file with a line `Final score: N/10` (the lowest of the seven); write the same rounds to QC-REVIEW.json as the QC rules say (the app shows them as a score card), and end your reply with one short line.

pipeline.title: Music and sound effects
pipeline.what: Claude picks the music; the app places it and the sound effects

action.label: Find music
action.prompt: Find three music tracks on mixkit.co that fit the film's mood and length and the style's sound palette (STYLE.md, the sound section: instruments, silences), and hand them to the app with the music_options tool (title, artist, its page on mixkit.co and the direct https://assets.mixkit.co/… .mp3 link). The app picks the first one for the film and places the sound effects; the owner can change both in the Final Mix. When the film already has a music track of the owner's, or the web is off for this project, say so in one line and change nothing.

pipeline.title: Tech checks
pipeline.what: Last of this stage, quiet: HyperFrames' check (layout, contrast, motion), Vietnamese letters, fonts, offline; the film is done when they pass

pipeline.title: Final Mix
pipeline.what: Optional: listen, then change the music or the sound effects (notes about the sound)
